overview: This table lists the items players can own or unlock, including clothing, player card parts, equipment, voices, poses, characters, and money.
description: Central catalog of inventory/shop/reward item rows (money, costumes, player-card parts, equipment, voice/pose unlocks, characters and story items), defining display text, type, cross-table links, stock rules, ordering, and progress unlock gates. Some rows are hidden/system entries rather than player-visible items.

Id.simple: The name that picks this item when it is given, bought, or checked.
Id.technical: FName row key used by stock counts, shop purchase grants, unlock checks, reward grants, and inventory-wide row collection. First-match helpers scan ItemDataTables in table order; full-row collectors iterate table order and then row-name order. The supplied export has 2,775 unique keys, including MONEY and ITM_*. Joins also arrive from CharacterVariation::Id_Item and ItemSet::Id_Item, whose entries are paired index-for-index with ItemSet::Quantity.

Id_ItemText.simple: Which word or phrase the game shows as this item's name.
Id_ItemText.technical: FName passed through GameItem_GetNameTextCore with the row's ItemType. Most types use the key directly; Money either formats Value directly (bWithValue false) or uses ITM_MONEY_1001 with an ITEM_VALUE parameter, while Costume/CustomVoice/SituationOverviewPose substitute fixed template keys and pass this key as an ITEM_NAME text parameter. Nickname keys are rewritten for the current language's TOP/BOTTOM suffix. None remains NAME_None for default types; archive text lists drop rows whose resolved text is empty, and where a parallel card row's Id_ItemText is None, title/nickname tiles substitute a generic label. The parallel PlayerCardTitle/PlayerCardNickname rows carry their own Id_ItemText labels and link back to Item::Id through Id_Item; their label requests do not read this field.

ItemType.simple: What kind of item this is, such as clothing, equipment, or a player card part. This decides where it appears and how it works.
ItemType.technical: EGameItemType (None=0, Money, ShortStory, Costume, Title, Nickname, Emblem, Plate, CursedTools, CursedObjects, Extras, CustomVoice, SituationOverviewPose, StoryDemoMovie, Character, Invalid=255), default None. It drives collection filtering, shop category grouping, icon sprite selection, previewability, money handling, ownership joins, and item-description behavior. Examples: Title..Plate are treated as player-card parts; CursedTools..Extras resolve equipment effects through EquipmentItemDataTable; Extras in the battle equipment slots are cleared and passed to ConsumeItem after their effects apply; Money bypasses per-item stock and uses user money. The export uses 13 of these values; StoryDemoMovie and Invalid are absent.

VariableId.simple: For some items, the name that connects this item to its equipment effect, card design, voice, pose, or story details.
VariableId.technical: FName whose target depends on ItemType. CursedTools/CursedObjects/Extras resolve EquipmentItemDataTable by VariableId and then EquipmentItemEffectDataTable by the equipment row's Id_EquipmentItemEffect[Index]; Emblem and Plate resolve PlayerCardEmblem/PlayerCardPlate rows; CustomVoice resolves CharacterCustomVoice; SituationOverviewPose resolves SituationOverviewPose rows; ShortStory's VariableId is the ShortStory row id used by Story_FindItemIdByVariableId_13022D0. Costume, Title, Nickname, Character and Money rows all have None in the export: costume joins through CharacterVariation::Id_Item == Item::Id, and title/nickname joins through the parallel rows' Id_Item == Item::Id. Shared helpers also find the first Item row with a given VariableId.

SortingOrder.simple: Where this item appears in lists. Bigger numbers put it later.
SortingOrder.technical: int32 at row offset 0x24, default 0. Collection archive tiles and title texts use TArray::Sort (not StableSort) by SortingOrder; player-card title/nickname lists use StableSort; shop lineups sort by the set's first item's value (GameShop_GetItemSetSortingOrder returns -1 when no item resolves); vs-enemy equipment tabs sort usable, used-up and unowned entries by it. The export has 2,768 unique nonzero values (1001-12016) plus seven 0 rows (MONEY and the six Character rows).

SellPrice.simple: The resale price recorded for this item. Its effect on the game is unclear.
SellPrice.technical: int32 serialized at row offset 0x28 with constructor default 0; exported values are 0, 2,000, 4,000, and 7,000. No identifiable C++ consumer reads this field in the available Source, and ShopLineupDataTable carries its own Price for purchases, so no sale formula or currency interaction can be asserted.

PossessionMax.simple: The most copies a player can hold. Bigger numbers allow more. Money is kept in the player's wallet.
PossessionMax.technical: int32 at row offset 0x2C, default 0. Purchase, initial-grant, and max-possession helpers clamp StudioItemStocks counts with FMath::Min(Count + Amount, PossessionMax). The confirmation dialog takes the first available set item's value as its purchase-limit basis and rejects confirmation when PurchaseCount + HaveCount exceeds it; shop list state marks an active lineup sold out when an item reaches the cap. Lottery conversion marks a draw replaced when the first item is at max. Exported values are 1, 99 (all Extras) and -1 (MONEY, which is handled through user money instead of item stock).

InitialPossession.simple: How many of this item a player starts with. Zero means none is given.
InitialPossession.technical: int32 at row offset 0x30, default 0. GameItem_GetInitialRows keeps rows with a positive value; GameItem_GrantInitialItems adds that amount to user money for Money rows or clamps it into StudioItemStocks for others, and the same row set is excluded from newly-owned collection achievements. Shop unlock-progress counters remove owned rows with UserProgressFlag < 0 and InitialPossession <= 0 as hidden/default starters; that predicate is not a purchase-availability test.

UserProgressFlag.simple: The game progress needed before this item becomes available. Items with no requirement are available right away.
UserProgressFlag.technical: int32 at row offset 0x34, default 0. Values below 0 mean no gate (unlocked); otherwise the flag encodes UserProgressFlagWords[Flag >> 2] bit (Flag & 3), with word indices >=128 treated as unreached. GameItem_IsRowUnlocked, GameItem_IsUnlocked, collection lists, shop progress checks, and rank/reward item-set display apply this same test. Exported values are -1, 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 7, 9 and 10.

notes: The supplied export contains one ItemDataTable with 2,775 rows and no duplicate IDs. The manager's ItemDataTables array can hold multiple tables and first-match helpers scan them in array order; if shards duplicate an ID, the earlier table shadows later rows. Full-row collectors iterate table order and then row-name order.

ItemDataTable is a hub: ItemSetDataTable::Id_Item points here and is paired index-for-index with Quantity; VariableId points outward to EquipmentItem/PlayerCard/Voice/Pose/ShortStory tables; CharacterVariation::Id_Item and parallel PlayerCardTitle/PlayerCardNickname::Id_Item point back here. Shop unlock and reward code resolves an ItemSet first and then reads its first contained Item row; GameShop_FindSetRowItem checks the requested index but still reads Id_Item[0], as documented in the reconstructed source.

The supplied export has 2,402 ItemSet rows with non-empty, equal-length Id_Item/Quantity arrays and every referenced item ID resolves; all equipment VariableIds resolve to 211 EquipmentItem rows, and all 162 voice and 162 pose VariableIds resolve to their target tables.

SellPrice is serialized but has no identified consumer. No Blueprint behavior is assumed; no retail Blueprint assets were reviewed, and the reconstruction's source states its Blueprints contain no game logic.
Only the supplied retail export and partial Content are available; no claim is made about all retail rows, DLC-specific tables, additional shards, or editor-only consumers.

usages.detail: GameItem_IsUnlocked begins the shared UserProgressFlag gate implementation (GameItem_IsRowUnlocked repeats it for a row pointer).
Filters owned stock entries by ItemType for inventory/player-card lists.
Grants InitialPossession amounts and clamps them by PossessionMax.
Builds the item name request from Id_ItemText and ItemType.
Chooses item icons by ItemType and resolves VariableId-linked plate/voice/pose art.
Uses VariableId to find EquipmentItem rows and their gameplay effects.
Filters unlocked rows by type and sorts by SortingOrder.
Applies the item progress gate, purchase clamp, and first-item SortingOrder/PossessionMax for shop sets.
Full-row collector walks ItemDataTables in table order and row-name order for inventory-wide scans.
Shared first-row helper returns the first matching Item row across the table array.
Resolves VariableId through EquipmentItemDataTable and indexes Id_EquipmentItemEffect for descriptions.
Reverse-joins owned Emblem/Plate items to PlayerCardEmblem/PlayerCardPlate rows by VariableId.
Reverse-finds the Item row whose VariableId equals a CharacterCustomVoice row id.
Treats situation-overview pose index 0 as free and requires an owned item matching VariableId for later poses.
Item-set alias checks the requested index but returns the progress-gated first contained Item row.
Rank rewards resolve the ItemSet first, then read its first Item row for type and image.
Boot calls GameItem_GrantInitialItems, consuming positive InitialPossession rows.
